## Purpose

Worktree custody owns every worktree from the moment it is reserved to the moment it is removed, so that no work a worker paid for is lost (G2). It decides when a worktree may be created, reused, rescued or removed, and it reconciles the ledger, the work directory and git on every pass. It serves task-execution, which gets a worktree for each leased task. It does not land or delete branches (integration) and does not decide task states (task-execution).

## Strategic classification

| Domain | Business model | Evolution |
|---|---|---|
| supporting | cost-reducer | custom |

_Strategize rationale_: supporting - G2 (no work a worker paid for is lost) depends on it; today's alternative is worktrees made by workers and orphaned on disk; rule 3 (diff 6, cplx 5); cplx 5 from 1 lifecycle of 8 states and 1 invariant (rescue ref written and read back before any removal, design I6); git does the work and is wrapped. Medium investment because a failure breaks G2 (A5). — _future_: Supporting, kept simple: a worktree row per lifecycle plus a reconciler against git worktree list. Fault-injection tests for rows 04 W6, W8, W9. No timeline to change.

## Domain roles

**execution-context** — It owns the worktree aggregate, whose lifecycle (reserved, created, landing, landed, orphaned, removed) protects invariant I6 and rescue rule RR-9. The clock and policies drive its 4 commands; no person commands it.

## Ubiquitous language

| Term | Meaning in this context | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| **Worktree** | The git working tree that fleetd leases to 1 task before it exists and never removes before its work is landed or rescued | checkout, workspace |
| **Rescue Ref** | A verified commit under refs/horch/rescue/ that saves the full state of a tree or an old branch tip before cleanup or rebase | backup, archive ref (a different ref family) |
| **Worktree Lease** | Same as Lease in this context: the worktree row that holds 1 worktree for 1 task and 1 owner. It is not the attempt lease of task-execution (decompose N4). | — |
| **Orphan** | A worktree, on disk or in git worktree list, that the ledger does not own or whose owner attempt is dead. It is adopted or rescued, never deleted. | — |
| **Lease** | The worktree lease: the ledger row written in the same transaction that leases the task, before the directory exists. It holds the worktree for 1 task until its work is landed or rescued | — |
| **Landed** | A worktree state: nothing in the worktree is unique any more, so fleetd may remove it (discover N6) | — |
| **Orphaned** | A worktree on disk with no live owner attempt, or with no ledger row | — |

## Business decisions

1. A worktree row is written in the same transaction that leases the task, before the directory exists. Only fleetd creates or removes worktrees (FR-11). A row left in reserved by a crash is created or dropped on the next pass.
2. No worktree is removed until its commits, its uncommitted files and its untracked files are saved on a rescue ref under refs/horch/rescue/, and that ref is read back and shown to hold them (RR-9). A rescue that fails verification leaves the tree in place and escalates the task.
3. Every pass compares the ledger with the work directory, and git worktree list every 60 s. A worktree on disk with no row, or with no live owner attempt, is adopted or rescued within 1 pass and never deleted (RR-10, I6).
4. Drop and cleanup refuse a dirty tree, a branch with a git stash entry, unpublished unique commits, and a HEAD that moved during the checks (04 W6).
5. Archive and trash refs only move forward, each ref write is read back before a folder is removed, and trash refs expire after 30 days (04 W8). Triage commits modified and untracked files before ARCHIVE or DELETE (04 W9).
6. A worktree survives attempts: a retry, a fallback restart or a resume reuses the same worktree (understand N1). The worktree goes to landing when its task branch is verified and to landed when the branch landed; only a landed or rescued worktree is removed (decompose N6).
7. An abandoned task branch is dropped only after worktree-rescued is recorded (connect N4). No git call runs inside a ledger transaction.
8. worktree-custody is the only caller of git worktree add, remove and list, and the only writer of rescue refs under refs/horch/rescue/. It runs no rebase, merge or branch delete; integration does ([define A26]).

## Assumptions

- [discover A6] The event order follows understand N7 (idea states), N8 (task branch states building, verifying, ready, in_bundle, landed with side states conflicted, gate_failed, abandoned) and N9 (worktree states reserved, created, active, landing, landed, orphaned, rescued, removed). (confidence high)
- [discover A7] 'Worktree landed' (nothing unique left) is folded into Task Branch Landed and Worktree Removed; it is not a separate event. (confidence medium)
- [discover A10] Event count 83 is above the standard band (25 to 60). The design has 4 state machines (idea, task, task branch, worktree) plus feature integration; merging them further hides the language conflicts H4 and H6. (confidence high)
- [discover A11] A state name is never written without the kind of its entity (design A20). The shared names stay: ready (task, task branch, feature) and landed (task branch, worktree). A task is done; its task branch is landed. (confidence high)
- [decompose A5] Worktree custody is its own context, not a part of integration, because the worktree lease and the no-loss rules differ from the branch landing rules. Decision D4, option A (orchestrator, D15). (confidence medium)
- [strategize A5] Worktree custody is supporting with medium investment. Its no-loss rule (rescue ref written and read back before any removal) is 1 invariant over a 8-state lifecycle, not an algorithm; a failure breaks G2, so it gets invariant tests and fault-injection tests. (confidence medium)
- [connect A8] git is called by 2 contexts, split by concern: worktree-custody for worktrees and rescue refs, integration for branches, merges, bundles and trial merges (orchestrator, D15). (confidence high)
- [organise A4] The data store is 1 SQLite ledger (~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3, WAL) plus the workspace files, both owned by the 1 deployable. Inside the ledger each context owns its tables: ideas owns ideas, requirements, questions; task-execution owns tasks, task_deps, task_covers, attempts, leases; worktree-custody owns worktrees; integration owns features, branches, gate_runs, trial_merges; fleet-runtime owns events and ingested; worker-profiles owns no table (its profiles are teammate files). Source: design Ledger schema with the aggregates of discover and decompose. (confidence medium)
- [define A9] 'conformist' guessed for external system clock (core contexts protect their model; others conform) - confirm
- [define A16] Business model cost-reducer.
- [define A21] Metric thresholds use the design's fixed values.
- [define A26] git has 2 callers: worktree-custody (worktrees, rescue refs) and integration (branches, merges).

## Verification metrics

- Business (G2): count of worktrees removed without being landed, merged or saved on a verified rescue ref. Target 0.
- Business (G2): passes in which an orphan worktree stays unadopted and unrescued after 1 pass. Target 0.
- Structural: count of git worktree add or remove calls outside the worktree-custody module, from arch_scan (FR-11). Target 0.

## Open questions

- [connect CC4 - coupling, medium] task-execution and worktree-custody depend on each other (R4 and R5): the worktree lifecycle follows the task lease and the attempt end, and launch waits for the worktree.
- [connect CC5 - coupling, medium] task-leased is an event, but task-execution cannot launch until the worktree exists, and a failed git worktree add must come back to task-execution. The event hides a command that needs a result.
- [connect CC6 - coupling, high] Trial merges, git worktree add and remove, and process starts are external calls. If one runs inside the ledger write transaction, a slow git or a hung process start holds the only writer.
- [connect CC7 - coupling, high] abandon-task-branch drops a task branch in integration, but the rescue ref that keeps the work is made in worktree-custody (04 W6). Both must happen, in order, or work is lost.
- [connect CC9 - coupling, low] task-branch-landed has 2 consumers that need different data: worktree-custody needs the task and worktree, ideas needs the feature and idea roll-up.

## Quality attributes

| Attribute | Priority | Requirement | Scenario |
|---|---|---|---|
| recoverability | high | No worktree is removed before its work is landed or on a verified rescue ref (RR-9, I6). | When a worker is killed with dirty and untracked files, then after cleanup the rescue ref holds every file, read back before removal. |
